title: Grande Prairie man dead following police involved shooting - Alberta police watchdog investigating
subtitle: "The Alberta Serious Incident Response Team (ASIRT) has been directed to investigate the circumstances surrounding the actions of the police during this investigation."
article: Wendel Houle, a 32-year-old resident of Grande Prairie, was killed in an RCMP-involved shooting Oct. 15, on the city's east side. As a result, the Alberta Serious Incident Response Team (ASIRT) is investigating.

Shortly after 7 p.m., police responded to a disturbance near 104 Avenue and 92A Street. They were met outside the residence by a male carrying a firearm. Approximately half an hour later, police issued a shelter-in-place order and asked the public to not post any information to social media.
The RCMP media release describes an altercation having happened between Houle and police and resulted in shots fired. Houle was struck and injured.
"Officers immediately provided first aid and EMS was called. The suspect was taken to hospital by EMS; however, the suspect later succumbed to his injuries."

RCMP notified the Director of Law Enforcement and ASIRT was directed to investigate. Additionally, the incident triggered an internal review process, separate from that of the province's overseer of investigations of police services.

"Independent of ASIRT's investigation, the RCMP's internal review process has been implemented to gather a full account of what took place during this incident. RCMP training, policy, police response, and the member's duty status will be subject to review."

ASIRT works independently of other police agencies. Its role is to investigate police officers involved in incidents causing death, or serious injury or where accusations of police misconduct warrant further review.
The agency provides answers to the public, police agencies, the provincial director of law enforcement and ultimately to the families of Affected Persons (AP).
